rationale: C24 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both orders allocate overlapping enemy-property functions among senior officers and then protect actions from jurisdictional challenges caused by that allocation. The child's unusually specific rule that an action is not invalid because it belonged to the Secretary of State rather than the Attorney General, or vice versa, closely tracks C24's provision barring challenges on the ground that action belonged to the Attorney General rather than the Treasury Secretary, or vice versa. C09 and C04 share relevant enemy-property transfer machinery, but neither matches this distinctive jurisdiction-saving structure as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It is the policy of this order that the Secretary of State, with the concurrence of the Attorney General, shall perform... and that the Attorney General, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State, shall perform...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is the policy of this order that administrative action under paragraph 1 hereof shall be taken by the Attorney General or any officer, person, agency, or instrumentality designated by him.
shared_material.explanation: Both use an express policy provision to allocate administration of property-related powers among designated officials.

shared_material.child_excerpt: However, no action taken hereunder by either the Secretary of State or the Attorney General shall be considered to be invalid on the ground that under the provisions of this order such action was within the jurisdiction of the Secretary of State rather than the Attorney General, or vice versa...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: No person affected by any... action issued or taken by either the Secretary of the Treasury or the Attorney General may challenge the validity thereof... on the ground that pursuant to the provisions of this Executive order, such... action was within the jurisdiction of the Attorney General rather than the Secretary of the Treasury or vice versa.
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive, materially parallel jurisdiction-saving clause, with the child substituting the Secretary of State for the Treasury Secretary and adapting the consequence from a bar on challenges to a declaration of validity.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Any money, property, or interest received as reimbursement... shall be administered and disposed of by the Attorney General as vested property pursuant to the said Trading With the Enemy Act, as amended.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Attorney General is hereby authorized and directed to take such action as he may deem necessary with respect to any property or interest of any nature whatsoever... [and] may exercise all powers and authority vested in the President by... the Trading With the Enemy Act, as amended.
shared_material.explanation: Both place administration of specified foreign or enemy-property interests with the Attorney General under Trading With the Enemy Act authority.
